answer: A refundable stake turns each identity into a slow-burning ember of commitment: newcomers lock a deposit before transacting, then earn signed receipts by completing small verifiable tasks checked by randomly assigned peers. Every receipt is hash-chained to the previous one, so a forged history echoes through the ledger and exposes the whole cluster at once. Trust accrues only from verified work, never from a velvet-smooth signup, so buying a pile of throwaway identities buys nothing: each fake must pay real stake and real time, and one contradiction slashes the deposit.
